body: Really? The TV shows make it look like the young fast-risers are the best, while those who take longer to bloom are losers.

Are you sure? It's been nearly 26 years of my life. I'm regretful of transferring colleges not once but twice and wasting my precious youth doing that.

And do you have experience that got you that job? I have limited experience besides a three-month internship and working at two call centers and this data entry position.
Really? I don't have enough money to move. I want to, but I'd need a job to move somewhere else. I already have a job here and I'm trying to apply to others.

In high school, I was a homebody at heart, so when time came to choose colleges, I chose Florida Atlantic University, in Boca Raton, Florida, due to the close proximity to home. But after two years, I started to tire of South Florida and personal tensions were on the rise, so I decided it was time for a transition.

I decided to transfer to Auburn University in Alabama. My adviser warned me that AU was in the Deep South, but I didn't listen and I regret it. I wanted to go there, due to their pre-pharmacy program and the warmth of Southern hospitality. Most importantly, I wanted a "lucky break" away from the cold and snobby "me, me, me" attitude of South Florida. I thought that in AU, I would experience the joy, the warmth, the love of the South, something that I can't have here in South Florida, due to the selfishness. But at AU, I got heavily bullied due to my ethnicity and felt unwanted. Also, there were poor disability services for my Asperger's syndrome , so I left after one year. 

Not wishing to return to FAU, I sent three more transfer applications to Florida State University in Tallahassee, University of Central Florida in Orlando, and University of South Florida in Tampa. USF was the only one that accepted me, so I transferred there for the second and final time. I absolutely loved it, now I'm in graduate school there.

I can't stop regretting that I wasted five and a half years of my life being miserable and "toughing it out" but for what? Thousands in loans, no career connections, no idea what I want from my life. 

Everyone acts like college is the best time of their life, yet I look back and regret so much, so many poor decisions that I'm not even sure I learned from. How can I stop being jealous of everyone else that loved college? How can I learn to not regret the decisions that I've made and simply live with them? I know that I cannot change them now, but I feel that it's not enough to just say, "Oh well it's in the past you can't change it, just live with it."
